terms.definition: The fourth Brāhmaṇa of the second adhyāya of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, centred on the dialogue between Yājñavalkya and Maitreyī.
terms.context: Swamiji presents this Brāhmaṇa as a new section whose beginning must be justified. Though Brahmavidyā has already been taught, this section brings in the importance of renunciation and a fresh entry into the same teaching through the question of what is truly dear.

terms.definition: The pratyagātmā — the inmost Self that cannot be objectified — is the subject matter (viṣaya) of brahmavidyā.
terms.context: Swamiji explains that brahmavidyā is not knowledge of some external Brahman but of oneself as Brahman. terms.definition: 'These three — name, form, and function — constitute everything that is.' (Bṛh. Up. 1.6.1)
terms.context: Swamiji uses this as the Upaniṣad's own summary of the manifest world. Whatever can be objectified has a name (nāma), a form (rūpa), and a function or action (karma). Brahman alone is beyond all three — it is sarvakāraṇam with no nāma-rūpa of its own. The Bhāṣya cites this verse to signal that the entire domain of avidyā has been covered by the first chapter.
